candidates.source_name: Ministrstvo za finance - predlog zakona o placilnih sredstvih / dostopnost gotovine (public consultation)
candidates.why_relevant: The single strongest forward-looking demand driver for this cell. The draft act on payment instruments, in public consultation as of this run, would oblige credit institutions and Posta Slovenije to maintain a sufficient network of cash points, require an ATM within 5 km of the centre of any settlement over 1,000 inhabitants, and let Banka Slovenije order a named bank to install an ATM or open a branch in an under-served area. If enacted (government reading expected September, possible adoption before year-end), it mechanically creates new ATM placements in a market that has been shrinking - a direct pipeline signal for every vendor in this cell. Consultation drafts also attract bank and association comments naming cost and equipment constraints.

negative_findings.description: No Slovenian country page, local legal entity, office or named Slovenian distributor could be found for Glory Global Solutions, Auriga SpA or KEBA, despite searches in both English and Slovenian. Diebold Nixdorf's indexed EMEA locations path for the region returned a 404-style title, suggesting the directory moved rather than that coverage ended.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned only global corporate pages and non-Slovenian references (KEBA references are Austrian/German Sparkassen and Erste; Auriga surfaced only via an ACI partner listing). CIMA was the exception - confirmed in Slovenia only indirectly, through distributor Demi Trade's catalogue.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: These vendors may serve Slovenia from Austrian, Italian or Croatian hubs or through unnamed agents, meaning their Slovenian footprint is invisible on their own web properties and must be established through the company register (AJPES), bank locator/equipment evidence and tender awards instead of vendor sites. Treat as 'not yet evidenced', not as 'absent from the market'.

negative_findings.description: No public tender or contract-award document for any Slovenian bank's ATM fleet purchase, renewal or maintenance was found on the public procurement portal or elsewhere.
negative_findings.result_summary: Procurement searches returned only the ZJN-3 legal framework and unrelated contracting authorities. No bank ATM notices surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is structural, not a search failure: Slovenian commercial banks are private entities and not contracting authorities under ZJN-3, so their ATM and self-service purchases are never published. Competitive intelligence in this cell therefore cannot rely on procurement records for the bank channel and must be reconstructed from installed-base observation (ATMinfo/locator diffs), service-partner disclosure and vendor press. The exception worth monitoring is Posta Slovenije and other state-linked buyers, which the draft cash-access law would draw into the cash-point obligation.

negative_findings.description: No Slovenian bank was found publishing the identity of its ATM hardware or service supplier in any press release, annual report page or news article located in this pass, including for NLB, the largest fleet owner.
negative_findings.result_summary: Targeted Slovenian searches on NLB ATM procurement returned only locator pages, general terms and mobile-branch marketing - no supplier, contract or vendor name.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Supplier attribution in this market must be inferred from second-order evidence: local service-partner customer logo walls (Demi Trade names NLB, NKBM, SKB and UniCredit), OEM press releases, and physical/photographic identification of machine models. Any vendor-share estimate built for Slovenia should be labelled as inferred, with its evidence chain recorded.

negative_findings.description: The Slovenian term 'bankomat' is heavily overloaded in consumer contexts and dominates search results with fee, locator and consumer-advice content, while the technically precise industry terms are far rarer.
negative_findings.result_summary: Consumer-facing pages crowded out supply-side results in nearly every 'bankomat' query. 'Recikliranje gotovine' as a Slovenian rendering of cash recycling returned essentially nothing supply-side; the market instead speaks of 'polog gotovine' and 'avtomatski polog'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Future collection should prefer the lower-noise supply-side vocabulary - 'bancni avtomat', 'upravljanje mreze bancnih avtomatov', 'samopostrezni terminal', 'bancna oprema', 'avtomatski polog gotovine', 'blagajniski sef', 'menjalni avtomat' - and should not expect a Slovenian-language equivalent of 'cash recycler' to exist as a marketing term.

negative_findings.description: Slovenian business press with the most likely supply-side reporting (Finance.si in particular) did not surface usable articles for this cell and is substantially subscription-gated.
negative_findings.result_summary: A targeted Finance.si-oriented query returned Delo, Monitor and Microsoft marketing pages instead of Finance.si articles, indicating either weak indexing or paywall exclusion.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Finance.si and similar B2B outlets are the most likely place a Slovenian bank's technology investment or supplier switch would be reported. A subscription and manual archive search should be treated as a required capability for this cell rather than assuming open-web coverage is sufficient.

coverage_gaps.description: The Bankart open-banking endpoint (openbanking.bankart.si) is only known second-hand, from ATMinfo.si's footer attribution. Its actual structure, access requirements and field set were not established in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch the portal root directly, look for a developer/API documentation section and any ATM-locator endpoint, and determine whether registration is needed. If it exposes structured per-ATM records including deposit capability, it should become the primary installed-base feed for this cell and demote HTML scraping to a fallback.

coverage_gaps.description: Glory Global Solutions - a major cash-recycling and teller-cash-automation competitor named in the cell brief - produced no Slovenian evidence at all, neither a country presence nor a local distributor.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run dedicated Glory-specific searches in Slovenian and Croatian, check Glory's own partner/distributor locator, and search AJPES for any Glory-related entity. Also check whether Glory reaches Slovenia via its Austrian or Italian organisation. Record the outcome explicitly either way so absence becomes an evidenced finding.

coverage_gaps.description: Cash-in-transit and cash-management companies (e.g. Varnost, Sintal, G4S-successor operations in Slovenia) were not investigated, yet they are the operational counterparties for ATM cash replenishment, smart safes and recycling economics, and frequently co-bid or co-deliver with hardware vendors.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Map Slovenian CIT/cash-management providers and their bank contracts; their service pages and references often disclose which ATM and smart-safe equipment they support, providing an independent read on the installed base.

coverage_gaps.description: Posta Slovenije was identified as a named cash-point obligor in the draft cash-access law but was not researched as a buyer of self-service and cash equipment. Unlike commercial banks, it is a state-owned entity and therefore likely a contracting authority publishing tenders.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Investigate Posta Slovenije's procurement pages and its notices on enarocanje.si for self-service kiosk, cash-handling and ATM-related tenders. This is potentially the only channel in this cell where full tender specifications and named contract winners are publicly obtainable.

coverage_gaps.description: No visual/physical identification source was established for determining which ATM makes and models are actually deployed at Slovenian sites - the most reliable way to attribute installed base when neither banks nor vendors disclose it.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assess whether street-level imagery, bank branch photography, ATMinfo location data joined with photographs, or community photo sources can support model-level identification, and define an ethical, ToS-compliant method before relying on it. Also check ATMIA or ECB-adjacent statistics for any make-level breakdown.

coverage_gaps.description: The Bankart annual report located is the 2019 edition; more recent annual reports and their ATM-count and partner disclosures were not retrieved.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate the current Bankart annual report archive and pull the most recent three editions to build a current ATM-count and partner time series, rather than relying on the 2019 figure of ~2,007 ATMs across six markets.

brief: Slovenia's ATM and self-service competitive arena is almost entirely undocumented at the transaction level - commercial banks are not contracting authorities, so no ATM tenders or supplier contracts are ever published, and no Slovenian bank was found naming its hardware or service supplier. Intelligence therefore has to be reconstructed from three usable layers: an unusually good installed-base observation layer (ATMinfo.si tracking ~1,046 ATMs per bank in near-real time, upstream of it a Bankart open-banking feed, and per-bank locators that flag deposit-capable units), a local-channel layer where competitors do reveal themselves (Demi Trade servicing NCR and Diebold fleets and distributing CIMA, with NLB/NKBM/SKB/UniCredit shown as customers; Biroservis Majer for cash-handling brands; Euronet running its own independent fleet), and an official layer at Banka Slovenije, which publishes the authoritative counts (1,284 ATMs at end-H2 2024, down 1.9%, ~74% contactless) and mandates reporting by ATM network operators. The decisive forward driver is the Ministry of Finance draft act on payment instruments now in public consultation, which would force cash-point coverage - an ATM within 5 km of any settlement over 1,000 people, with Banka Slovenije able to order a named bank to install one - reversing a shrinking estate into mandated deployment. Global OEM sites are weak for this cell: Glory, Auriga and KEBA show no Slovenian trace, Diebold Nixdorf's regional locations directory appears to have moved, and their local presence must be established via AJPES, distributor catalogues and installed-base evidence rather than their own web properties.
